args.summary: Decision: PROMOTE, recorded in review/C-dashboard-5/decision.json (written in step 1; write_file is no longer available this turn, so the existing file stands). Evidence: canary v1.1 served 2411/9785 reqs (~25% share, real sample); 0 5xx and 0.00% err% on both arms in aggregate and in every 30s window; canary p50/p95/p99 34/93/105 ms vs stable 34/94/104 ms; per-route parity on /browse (22/27 both), /search (47/59/61 both) and /checkout (82/104/107 vs 81/103/105); no degradation trend over time (canary p95 92/92/93/96 vs stable 94/94/95/92). Judgement: the only blemishes are canary /browse p99 77 ms vs stable 28 ms and a 4 ms p95 gap in the last window - a thin single-pod tail that does not move overall p99 (105 vs 104) and sits within stable's own 92-95 ms jitter, so neither trips an error or latency gate; blocking the release would be the costlier error. Recommend watching /browse p99 after scale-out, since one pod is a weak basis for tail estimates.
